Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:1.hebrew: ורבנן - אין הכי נמי, דההיא ודאי מיבעי ליה להכי, דממכרו ולא שנת מנין עולם; ו"ימים" מיבעי ליה למעת לעת, שאם מכרה באחד בניסן בחצי היום, אין מונין לו שנה עד שיגיע חצי היום של אחד בניסן הבא:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:1.english: And the Rabbis - Indeed, that [phrase] is certainly needed for that [purpose], [namely,] that [it is a year] from his sale and not a year of the counting of the world; and [the word] "days" is needed for [counting] from hour to hour, [meaning] that if he sold it on the first of Nisan at midday, one does not count a [full] year for him until midday of the following first of Nisan arrives:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:2.hebrew: ר' יהודה היא - דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר, דרבית הבאה ע"י מכר קרי צד אחד, משום דאין בא לידי רבית משני צדדין; שאם לא יגאלנה ותיחלט לו, אין כאן רבית, אבל הלואה ודאי באה לידי רבית, שאינה נחלטת לעולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:2.english: It is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda - who says [that] one-sided interest is permitted; for interest that comes through a sale is called "one-sided" because it does not result in interest on both sides [i.e., in both possible outcomes]. For if he does not redeem it and it becomes permanently his [i.e., the buyer's], there is no interest here; whereas a [regular] loan certainly results in interest, since it is never forfeited permanently:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:3.hebrew: ועשה לו שדהו מכר - שמשכן לו שדהו על אותו מנה, וכתב לו: "אם לא אתן לך מנה מיכן ועד שלש שנים, הרי היא שלך":
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:3.english: And made his field a sale to him - [meaning] that he pledged his field to him for that maneh, and wrote to him: "If I do not give you [the] maneh between now and three years [from now], behold, it is yours":

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:4.english: When the seller consumes produce - [during] all those years, it is permitted:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:5.hebrew: לוקח אוכל פירות אסור - שמא יגאלנה בתוך שלש, ונמצא שאכלם ברבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:11:5.english: [If] the buyer consumes the produce, it is prohibited - lest [the seller] redeem [the field] within three [years], and it turns out that [the buyer] consumed [the produce] as interest:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:12:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה היא - דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר. דרבית הבאה ע"י מכר קרי "צד אחד", משום דאין בא לידי רבית משני צדדין: שאם לא יגאלנה ותיחלט לו, אין כאן רבית; אבל הלואה ודאי באה לידי רבית, שאינה נחלטת לעולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:12:1.english: [The Mishnah] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda - who says [that] one-sided interest is permitted. For interest that comes about through a sale is called "one-sided" because it does not result in interest from both sides: for if [the seller] does not redeem it and it becomes permanently [the buyer's], there is no interest here; whereas a loan certainly results in interest, since [the field] never becomes permanently [the lender's]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:12:2.english: An incident involving Baitos ben Zunin - We read [this in the text]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:13:1.hebrew: צד אחד ברבית - שאם יגאלנה יהא רבית, ואם לאו לא יהא רבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:13:1.english: One-sided interest - [Meaning] that if he redeems it, it will be interest, and if not, it will not be interest:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:1:1.hebrew: תני חדא - במקדיש שדה אחוזה, לוה וגואל; היינו הך דקתני לעיל: "אם גאל יגאל, מלמד שלוה וגואל כו'", ור"ש קאמר לה, ואידך רבנן דפליגי עליה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:1:1.english: It is taught [in] one [baraita] - Regarding one who consecrates an ancestral field, [one may] borrow and redeem; this is the same [teaching] that was taught above: "If he will indeed redeem — this teaches that one may borrow and redeem, etc." And Rabbi Shimon stated it, while the other [baraita is the view of] the Rabbis who disagree with him:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:2:1.hebrew: הרי זה גואל מיד - ואין לו דין שדה אחוזה, שצריך להמתין שתי שנים:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:2:1.english: He may redeem [it] immediately - And it does not have the law of an ancestral field, [where] one must wait two years:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:2:2.hebrew: הרי זה כמין רבית - שכשמחזיר לו מעותיו בתוך שנה, ואין זה מנכה לו כלום, נמצא שנשתמש בביתו בשכר המתנת מעותיו:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:2:2.english: This is like a form of interest - For when [the seller] returns his money to him within a year, and this [buyer] does not deduct anything for him, it turns out that he [the buyer] used his [the seller's] house as payment for waiting for his money:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:2:3.hebrew: ואינה רבית - גמורה, דרבית לא מיקרי אלא ע"י הלואה ולא ע"י מכר:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:2:3.english: And it is not interest - full-fledged [interest], for [something] is only called interest [when it is] through a loan, and not through a sale:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:3:1.hebrew: יגאל בנו - בתוך שנה אם ירצה, אבל לאחר שנה נחלט ואינו נגאל עוד לעולם, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:ל׳): "ואם לא יגאל עד מלאת לו שנה וגו'":
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:3:1.english: His son may redeem [it] - within [the] year if he wishes, but after a year it becomes permanently transferred [to the buyer] and can never be redeemed again, as it is written (Leviticus 25:30): "And if it is not redeemed until a year is completed for him, etc.":

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:3:2.hebrew: אלא משעה שנמכר - שאם מכרה ראובן לשמעון בניסן ושמעון ללוי באייר, כיון שהגיע ניסן הבא נחלט, ואין מונין למכר שני אלא לראשון:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:3:2.english: Only from the time that it was sold - For if Reuven sold it to Shimon in Nisan, and Shimon [sold it] to Levi in Iyar, once the following Nisan arrives it becomes permanently vested [in the buyer], and we do not count [the year] from the second sale, but rather from the first:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:3:3.english: As it is stated: "until the completion of a year for him" - [This] implies [that] we count [the year] for this one whose ancestral property it was:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:4:1.hebrew: את חדש העיבור - שאם היתה שנה מעוברת, אינה נחלטת עד שלשה עשר חדש:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:4:1.english: The intercalated month - [Meaning] that if it was a leap year, [the house] does not become [the buyer's] in perpetuity until thirteen months [have passed]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:4:2.hebrew: שנה ועיבורה - בין בשנה פשוטה בין בשנה מעוברת, נותנין לו שנת לבנה וימים שיתירים בשנת חמה על שנת לבנה — אחד עשר יום, שמהם אנו מעברים את השנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:4:2.english: A year and its addition - Whether in an ordinary year [or] in a leap year, we give him a lunar year and the days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year — eleven days, from which we intercalate the year:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:4:3.hebrew: ואחד הניתן במתנה - אם רצה נותן לגאול בתוך שנתו, יגאל, ואם לאו, חלוט לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:4:3.english: And one to whom it is given as a gift - If the giver wishes to redeem [it] within its year, he may redeem [it], and if not, it is permanently [the recipient's].

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:5:1.hebrew: מתני' - דקתני "הרי זה גואל מיד", דמשמע אפי' בו ביום שמכרה מותר לגאול, דלא כרבי:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:5:1.english: The Mishnah - which teaches, "he may redeem [it] immediately," implying [that] even on the very day he sold it, it is permitted to redeem [it], is not in accordance with Rabbi:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:7:1.english: For days shall its redemption be, and “days” are not fewer than two - so that it [the house] does not remain in the possession of the buyer for less than two days:

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:9:1.hebrew: מיום ליום - שאם מכרה באחד בניסן, אין מונין שנה למנין עולם, דלימא: כיון שהגיע תשרי עלתה לו שנה, שהרי יצתה אותה שנה; אלא עד אחד בניסן הבא אינו נחלט:
Rashi on Arakhin 31a:9:1.english: From day to day - [This means] that if one sold it on the first of Nisan, we do not count the year according to the calendar of the world, such that one would say: "Once Tishrei has arrived, a year has been counted for him, for that year has ended"; rather, until the first of the next Nisan it does not become permanently [the buyer's].

Rashi on Arakhin 31a:9:2.english: The year of its sale - and not [a year] of the reckoning of the world:

Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:10:1.hebrew: והתניא הרי זו רבית גמורה אלא שהתורה התירתו - ומסיק רבי יוחנן: הא ר' יהודה, הא רבנן. פירוש: מתני' כר' יהודה, דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר; וברייתא דתני "רבית גמורה", אתיא כרבנן. וא"ת: מאי שנא ממשכנתא בלא נכייתא, דאינו אלא אבק רבית, כדאיתא באיזהו נשך (ב"מ דף סב. ושם): א"ל רבינא, והרי משכנתא בלא נכייתא, דבדיניהם מוציאין מלוה למלוה ובדיננו אין מחזירין ממלוה ללוה, אלמא לאו רבית גמורה היא, והכא אמר דהוי ריבית גמורה? ולפי פירוש רש"י דמחלק בין שדה לבית, ניחא. גבי הא דתנן פרק איזהו נשך (בבא מציעא סד:): המלוה את חבירו לא ידור בחצרו חנם ולא ישכור ממנו בפחות (ממנו) [מפני] שהוא רבית; ופירש רש"י שם: מאי שנא ממשכנתא דנכייתא דשרי? ותירץ: דיש לחלק בין שדה לבית, דשמא השדה לא יעשה פירות, אבל הבית אי אפשר שלא יהנה ממנו בדירתו, ומשום הכי כי מנכה לו מן השכירות הוי רבית. ולפי זה ניחא נמי הכא, דבית שהוא דר בו בלא ספק, הוי רבית גמורה; אבל שדה, דשמא לא יעשה פירות, כי אכיל ליה נמי בלא נכייתא, לאו רבית גמורה היא. ואין נראה לר"ת חילוק זה, דבבית נמי איכא ספיקא, שמא יפול או ישרף. אלא ודאי אין חילוק בין שדה לבית; וההיא דמלוה את חבירו לא ישכור ממנו בפחות, יש לתרץ דלא דמי למשכנתא בנכייתא דשרי, דההיא משכנתא מיירי שהלוה לו על השדה, ואין הלוה יכול להשכירו לאחר מפני שהוא ביד המלוה, משום הכי אינו רבית, דהא בלאו הכי הוא בטל; והא דתנן "המלוה את חבירו לא ישכור ממנו בפחות", מיירי שלא הלוה לו על שדה או על הבית, וביד הלוה להשכירו לאחר, נמצא כשמוזיל גביה, רבית הואי. ולפי' זה דר"ת, אינו מחלק בין שדה לבית, הדרא קושיא לדוכתיה: מאי שנא ממשכנתא בלא נכייתא, דלא חשבינן ליה רבית גמורה? וצ"ל דרבית גמורה מדרבנן קאמר; והאי דאמר "אלא שהתורה התירתו", הכי פירושו: מדכתב לן רחמנא דין בתי ערי חומה, גלי לן דכי ה"ג אין זה רבית דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:10:1.english: But isn’t it taught [in a baraita]: This is fully [considered] interest, but the Torah permitted it? - And Rabbi Yoḥanan concludes: This [Mishna] is [according to] Rabbi Yehuda, and this [baraita] is [according to] the Rabbis. Meaning: our Mishna is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says that a one-sided [possibility of] interest is permitted; whereas the baraita, which teaches [that it is] "full interest," follows the Rabbis. And if you ask: What is different [here] from a pledge [of property] without deduction [from the debt], which is only "dust of interest" [rabbinic interest], as is [stated] in [the chapter] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 62a and there [in the gemara]): "Ravina said to him: But behold a pledge without deduction, where in their [non-Jewish] courts they exact [it] from the borrower for the lender, whereas in our courts we do not return [it] from the lender to the borrower" — thus, it is not full interest; yet here [the baraita] says that it is full interest? According to the explanation of Rashi, who distinguishes between a field and a house, it is resolved. Regarding that which we learned in the chapter Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 64b): "One who lends to his fellow may not dwell in his courtyard for free, nor may he rent from him for less [than the normal rate], because it is interest," Rashi explained there: What is different [in that case] from a pledge with deduction, which is permitted? And he answered: One must distinguish between a field and a house, for perhaps the field will not produce crops, whereas [with] a house it is impossible that he will not benefit from it by dwelling in it; therefore, when he deducts [only a small amount] from the rent for him, it is interest. According to this, here too it is resolved: for a house in which he dwells without any doubt is full interest; whereas a field, which perhaps will not produce crops, even when he eats [its produce] without deduction, it is not full interest. However, this distinction does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for in a house too there is uncertainty, lest it collapse or burn down. Rather, certainly there is no distinction between a field and a house. And that [case of] "one who lends to his fellow may not rent from him for less" can be resolved [by saying] that it is not comparable to a pledge with deduction, which is permitted: for that [case of] a pledge refers to where he lent him [money] against the field, and the borrower cannot rent it to someone else because it is in the lender’s possession; therefore it is not interest, since even without this it would stand idle. Whereas that which we learned, "one who lends to his fellow may not rent from him for less," refers to where he did not lend him [money] against the field or against the house, and it is in the borrower’s power to rent it to someone else; thus, when he lowers the price for him, it is interest. According to this [explanation] of Rabbeinu Tam, [since] he does not distinguish between a field and a house, the question returns to its place: What is different [here] from a pledge without deduction, which we do not consider full interest? And one must say that [when the baraita says] "full interest," it means [full interest] by rabbinic decree; and that which it says, "but the Torah permitted it," this is its explanation: since the Merciful One wrote for us the law of houses of a walled city, He revealed to us that in a case like this it is not biblical interest:

Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:13:1.hebrew: ור' יהודה סבר צד אחד ברבית מותר - וא"ת, לר' יהודה משכנתא בלא נכייתא נמי תישתרי, דצד אחד בריבית הוא, ושמא לא יפדנו עוד! וי"ל, דלא חשבינן צד אחד ברבית אלא כגון עשה לו שדהו מכר, דאיכא צד מכר אם לא יפדנו בתוך הזמן הקבוע לו; אבל משכנתא בלא נכייתא, דליכא ביה צד מכר, דלעולם הוא ביד הלוה לפדותו, ואם יפדנו, כיון שאין מנכה לו מן הפירות שאכל, הוה ליה רבית — מידי דהוה אמלוה סאה בסאה, ולא חשיב ליה ר' יהודה צד אחד ברבית אף על גב דשמא לא יתייקר; מ"מ כיון דאין בו צד מכר אסור, ולא חשיב ליה ר"י צד אחד ברבית:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:13:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds that uncertain interest is permitted - And if you say: According to Rabbi Yehuda, a mortgage without deduction [from the principal] should also be permitted, since it is [a case of] uncertain interest, as perhaps [the borrower] will never redeem it! And one can answer: We do not consider [a transaction to be] uncertain interest except in a case such as where he made his field a sale to him, where there is an aspect of sale if he does not redeem it within the time fixed for him; but a mortgage without deduction, where there is no aspect of sale in it — since it is always in the borrower's power to redeem it, and if he redeems it, since [the lender] does not deduct for him from the produce that he ate, it is interest — is just like one who lends a se'ah for a se'ah, which Rabbi Yehuda does not consider [a case of] uncertain interest even though perhaps [the grain] will not rise in price; nevertheless, since there is no aspect of sale in it, it is prohibited, and Rabbi Yehuda does not consider it uncertain interest:

Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:1:1.hebrew: תני חדא לוה וגואל לחצאין - פירש רש"י דאמקדיש שדה אחוזה קאי, ול"נ, דא"כ הוי סתם מתני' דתנן "בהקדש מותר בכולן" כר"ש ולא כרבנן. ואור"י דקאי אמוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה, וכן מוכחת הסוגיא בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כא. ושם כ:), אבל מקדיש שדה אחוזה — אפי' רבנן מודו דלוה וגואל לחצאין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:1:1.english: It is taught [in] one [baraita]: One may borrow and redeem, [and redeem] in halves - Rashi explained that it refers to one who consecrates an ancestral field. But this does not seem [correct], for if so, the anonymous Mishnah — where we learned, "Regarding consecrated [property], all of them are permitted" — would be in accordance with Rabbi Shimon and not in accordance with the Rabbis. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that it refers to one who sells a house in a walled city, and so too the sugya in the first chapter of Kiddushin (21a, and there 20b) indicates; whereas [regarding] one who consecrates an ancestral field, even the Rabbis concede that one may borrow and redeem, [and redeem] in halves:

Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:1:2.hebrew: תניא בת"כ גבי מוכר שדה אחוזה, "וחשב שני ממכרו": שנים אתה מחשב, ואי אתה מחשב חדשים; ומנין אם רצה לעשות חדשים שנה יעשה? ת"ל: "וחשב". וא"ת: היכי מצינו ששניהם לצורך המוכר, שיהא בו ריוח למוכר? בשלמא כשמחשב חדשים מצינו, כגון שבא לגאלה באמצע השנה, דמחשבינן ליה חדשים שעברו שאכל הלוקח לגרע פדיונו, כמו שאנו מחשבין השנים שעברו שאכל הלוקח; אבל "אי אתה מחשב חדשים" היכי משכחת לה? ויש לומר דמשכחת ליה כגון אם מכר בניסן בעשרה ליטרין ומחצה, ויש עד היובל י' שנים ומחצה, ובא לגואלה בר"ה, ויש עוד להבא עד היובל ה' שנים:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:1:2.english: It was taught in Torat Kohanim regarding one who sells an ancestral field, [on the verse] "And he shall calculate the years of its sale": You calculate years, and you do not calculate months; and from where [do we derive that] if he wishes to make months into a year, he may do so? The Torah states: "And he shall calculate." And if you ask: How do we find that both [options] are for the benefit of the seller, such that there is a profit for the seller in it? Granted, when one calculates months we find [this], such as when he comes to redeem it in the middle of the year, where we calculate for him the months that have passed during which the buyer ate [the produce] to deduct [from] his redemption [price], just as we calculate the years that have passed during which the buyer ate [the produce]; but [the case of] "you do not calculate months" — how do you find it [to be to the seller's benefit]? And one can say that you find it, for example, if he sold [it] in Nisan for ten and a half litrin, and there are ten and a half years until the Jubilee, and he comes to redeem it on Rosh Hashanah, and there are still five years remaining ahead until the Jubilee:

Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:9:1.hebrew: מיום ליום ומעת לעת מעד תום שנת ממכרו נפקא - במס' נדה דף מז: ושם ד"ה כולן) פירש ה"ר ר' אלחנן, דדוקא בבתי ערי חומה בעינן מעת לעת [לשעות], אבל אינך דהתם, דמצי למימר דאזלינן בהן בתר שנים שלהם ולא בתר שנות עולם, בכולהו לא בעינן מעת לעת [לשעות], דבבתי ערי חומה דוקא הוא דגלי ליה קרא, אבל דאינך לא. והתוס' כתבו כאן: הוא הדין בכולהו בעינן מעת לעת [לשעות], דילפינן שנה [שנה] מבתי ערי חומה, כדאמר הש"ס לקמן גבי מילתא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31a:9:1.english: From day to day and from hour to hour is derived from "until the completion of the year after it is sold" - In tractate Niddah (47b, s.v. "Kulan"), Rabbi Elchanan explained that specifically regarding houses of walled cities do we require a full twenty-four-hour period [down to the hours]; however, [regarding] those other cases there [in Niddah], where one can say that we follow their own years rather than calendar years of the world, in all of them we do not require a full twenty-four-hour period [down to the hours], for it is specifically regarding houses of walled cities that Scripture revealed it, whereas regarding those other cases, [it did] not. And Tosafot wrote here [that] the same law applies to all of them: we require a full twenty-four-hour period [down to the hours], because we derive [a verbal analogy of] "year" [and "year"] from houses of walled cities, as the Gemara says later regarding another matter:
